title: Journalist Among Eight Palestinians Killed in Israeli Attacks on Gaza
excerpt: Palestinian journalist Muhammad Abdel Aziz al-Najjar, the 263rd media worker killed since October 2023, died as Israeli strikes hit a Gaza City van, an apartment, and a displaced-persons shelter amid continued ceasefire violations.
body:
• At least eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Wednesday, including journalist Muhammad Abdel Aziz al-Najjar, according to Gaza's Government Media Office and medical sources.
  • Al-Najjar was the 263rd Palestinian journalist killed since October 2023, the media office said; on Thursday, Israel's military said he was killed in a Khan Younis airstrike a day earlier and claimed he was a Hamas operative who took part in the October 7 attack — claims that could not be independently verified.
  • Separately, six people died when an Israeli drone struck a passenger van in Tal al-Hawa, southwest Gaza City; 13 wounded were taken to al-Quds Hospital, with medical sources describing injuries as critical.
  • The strikes come as Israel continues to violate a nearly year-old ceasefire agreed in October 2025, with Palestinian health authorities saying at least 1,431 Palestinians have been killed since the truce took effect.

At least eight Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip, as Israel continues to violate a nearly year-old ceasefire. Palestinian journalist Muhammad Abdel Aziz al-Najjar was among those killed on Wednesday, Gaza's Government Media Office said, without providing the location or circumstances of the attack. Al-Najjar was the 263rd journalist killed by Israel since October 2023, the office said.

Separately, six people were killed on Wednesday by an Israeli drone attack on a passenger van in Tal al-Hawa, a neighborhood in southwest Gaza City, according to witnesses and medical sources. The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its crews took 13 wounded people to al-Quds Hospital. Medical sources told Al Jazeera the injuries were "critical."

Context & Background

The violence is part of a continuing pattern despite the ceasefire agreed last October. Earlier, the official Palestinian Wafa news agency reported an Israeli attack on a residential apartment near al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City killed at least one woman. Elsewhere, four Palestinians, including two children, were wounded when an Israeli drone hit a shelter for displaced people in southern Gaza, according to local sources cited by Wafa. Two other Palestinians were seriously wounded southeast of Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, while Israeli tank fire was reported in southern Khan Younis.

On Thursday, the Israeli military said al-Najjar had been killed in an airstrike in Khan Younis a day earlier, asserting that he belonged to Hamas's military wing, participated in the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, and had recently been involved in organizing attacks and rebuilding the group's military capabilities. Those assertions could not be independently verified.

According to Palestinian health authorities, at least 1,431 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since the truce took effect. One Palestinian commentator told Al Jazeera that since the ceasefire was signed in October 2025, there have been more than 5,000 violations by the Israeli military, leaving residents afraid to walk the streets.

Impact & Analysis

The death toll among journalists remains one of the war's most documented features: 263 media workers killed in roughly three years, according to Gaza's media office. Israel has repeatedly claimed that individuals counted as journalists were militants — a pattern advocacy groups dispute and say requires independent investigation. The Committee to Protect Journalists recently revised its own Gaza casualty database, removing 19 people previously classified as journalists after determining they were militants or combat participants, following an internal audit.

Al Jazeera's Hind Khoudary reported from Gaza City that doctors warned it was difficult to save the wounded "because the health system is decimated by years of Israeli attacks and the blockade," and the death toll could rise. On the same day, mourners held a mass funeral for the remains of 105 people recovered from an earlier attack — the fifth-largest such recovery since the war began.

Analysts say the international community has been unable to hold Israel accountable or restrain it in Gaza, as the truce framework — which envisioned an international security force — has failed to materialize.

Diaspora Angle

The killing of journalists in Gaza resonates strongly in India's vast media community and its large diaspora, where press-freedom advocates have long followed the war's toll on media workers. India's news ecosystem — among the world's largest — covers Gaza closely, and the mounting journalist death count has drawn condemnation from press bodies worldwide, including Indian journalists' organizations that have demanded international accountability.

What's Next

With violations continuing almost daily, there is no indication the strikes will stop. Medical officials warn the wounded may yet die, and the question remains whether any international mechanism will enforce the truce — or whether the "ceasefire" exists in name only.
